scope: Historical local package metadata and selected source-claim reconciliation, not acceptance, full ledger replay or validity certification.

score_critical_premise.statement: Only first blocks whose chaining value is in the class ((cv0 >> 24) & 63) == 12 are kept (2^-6 of them; proof.md Section 3.8). (a) Under H1 a kept chaining value has cv[0] uniform in the class and its other words uniform; for the claws of a kept chaining value C1, C2 and G pass at the rates of H1-P1 (they do not read the chaining value), and F7 passes at the class average of the F7 rate over the good-pair law of q, charged at its one-sided 99% lower bound F7R = 0.11985 (the step-3b cost at the upper bound 0.12136). (b) Given the message-difference profile of a good pair (both members' W16..W37), the state part of acceptance is the same for good pairs with cv[0] uniform in the class as for those with cv[0] uniform (the law of H2-P1 and H8). The message part is measured and charged: the class's good pairs are accepted with probability at least 2^-0.0225 x 2^MSG_LO q3r = 2^-0.0693 q3r, and their average acceptance satisfies the weak upper form a-bar <= 2^10 q3r used in Lemma T.
score_critical_premise.scope: q_pf and q3r in N_CV and the step-3b cost term: the class raises q_pf by 0.11985 / 0.0668945 = 2^0.8413 and, after the charged message factor and the class test (3 operations per first block), gives time_log2 77.1297 (3eec1f5a without the class: 77.9182).
score_critical_premise.extrapolation: Argument (proof.md Section 3.8): F7 is the only post-filter that reads the chaining value (W7 = KK7c + q, KK7c contains -cv[0] once); its membership depends on the high bits of W7 and the good pairs' q is not uniform, so the F7 rate averaged over q depends on cv[0] (H1-P1's overdispersion across chaining values). cv[0] = A_-1 is read only by steps 0..3 and A2..A15, E6..E15 are S's words, so the class reaches rows 16..37 only through the message words. Evidence: (a) clsamp.c (own C, peak 7,880 KiB): for each of 2^20 G-passing q drawn by sel_rates' law, F7 tested for 16 cv[0] uniform in each of the 64 classes and 16 over all words; the class was chosen as the best of 64 on one pool (0.1207520, next 0.1180669) and read on an independent pool: 0.1206148, against 0.0668707 over all cv[0] (|F7|/2^32 = 0.0668945); each per-q average lies in [0, 1], so the one-sided 99% bounds are 0.11987 and 0.12135. (b) msample.c (own C, H8's exact good-pair sampler, a0 in SEL on both sides, the second side with cv[0] in the class), 10^8 good pairs per side over four seeds: profile 15,164 vs 15,333, dW23 XOR 12,498,809 vs 12,498,782, dW25 229,398 vs 228,730, E16 check failures 0; log2 ratio +0.0160, one-sided 99% lower bound -0.0225, charged. (c) Organizer trials: utab-online-r38 trial 8 re-samples the class's F7 rate against all cv[0]; utab-rows-r38 trial 5 runs the sampler at reduced size with E16 and the post-filter flags of every pair checked on the real words.
score_critical_premise.limitations: The state part of rows 16..37 is not measurable at this probability; H9 assumes it unchanged given the message profile, as H8 does for the window. The class's F7 rate rests on a pool of 2^20 q with 16 sampled cv[0] each; the organizer trial re-samples it at reduced size.

publication_boundary: The CV-selection principle was already used in a stored six-bit-class package. Its changed-law H9 is explicitly declared; the current 70-row single-CV recount neither validates that premise nor creates a new attack score.
